headline: US Treasury yields hit fresh highs on 24 September, with the 10 year closing at 5.162 percent and the 30 year at its highest since 2004, pushing October Fed hike odds above 75 percent and dragging Nifty 50 down 1.64 percent even as US stocks finished flat.

summary.us: The S&P 500 closed 24 September down 0.02 percent at 7,704.13 and the Nasdaq Composite rose 0.01 percent to 26,939.37, after a Reuters report that Tehran could allow navigation through the Strait of Hormuz in exchange for an end to the US naval blockade pulled oil off its session highs and let stocks trim losses. The 10 year Treasury yield ended at 5.162 percent and the 30 year reached its highest since 2004 as the September flash PMI showed the fastest private sector growth in more than five years, lifting October Fed hike odds above 75 percent on CME FedWatch; Oracle fell 3.47 percent and Arm 7.88 percent on the Project Jupiter force majeure notice, while Meta rose 4.50 percent on JPMorgan's Muse upgrade.
summary.india: Nifty 50 fell 1.64 percent to 23,063.10 and Bank Nifty dropped 1.96 percent to 55,438.50 after IRDAI published a consultation paper on insurance distribution economics proposing hard commission caps, which erased about Rs 1.12 lakh crore of market value across 12 financial stocks; PB Fintech fell 36 percent, HDFC Life 6.16 percent, Bajaj Finance 5.87 percent and Axis Bank 4.56 percent. Reliance Industries added to the drag with a 2.31 percent fall to a 17 month low on rating agency concerns about its core segments, FIIs sold Rs 5,027 crore of cash equities against DII buying of Rs 4,301 crore, India VIX jumped 22.61 percent and the rupee sat near 95.95 per dollar with traders citing RBI intervention around the 96 handle ahead of the 5 to 7 October MPC meeting.
summary.global: Tokyo reopened after the Silver Week break and the Nikkei 225 gained, while the Hang Seng slipped 0.29 percent and mainland benchmarks posted their biggest one day fall in a month as investors doubted the Trump and Xi meeting in Washington would deliver more than the two month trade truce extension to 10 January that Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent confirmed. Europe closed lower with the DAX down 0.57 percent and the FTSE 100 down 0.24 percent, Brent crude gained 3.4 percent to 106.60 dollars after Houthi missile fire at Saudi targets before paring on the Hormuz report, and US natural gas jumped 8.04 percent on a sixth consecutive light EIA storage injection.

weekly.narrative: The week belonged to central banks. The Federal Reserve raised rates a quarter point on 16 September to 3.75 to 4 percent, its first hike since 2023, and the Bank of Japan followed on 18 September with a split 7 to 2 vote that lifted its policy rate to a 31 year high of 1.25 percent, yet the yen weakened past 156 per dollar because two board members dissented and Governor Ueda made no commitment to further moves. US equities finished mixed as the 10 year Treasury yield came back to about 5 percent after touching a 19 year high above 5.04 percent ahead of the Fed, with the Dow down 1.69 percent on the week while the Nasdaq Composite added 0.72 percent. India was the weak spot, where the Nifty and Sensex logged a sixth consecutive weekly decline, the longest losing run in six years, under crude above 100 dollars, tighter global policy and a deepening Tata Sons governance dispute. Metals held their ground, with copper up about 2 percent on the week as the Yangshan import premium climbed 72 percent in September to a near four year high and silver adding 3.46 percent, while crypto turned sharply higher into the weekend on post Fed relief and rotation into altcoins. Next week brings S&P Global flash PMIs on 23 September, a heavy run of Fed speakers, Costco and Nike earnings on 24 September, and in India the Varmora Granito, Elevate Campuses, ArMee Infotech and A-One Steels offers alongside the close of the NSE IPO on 21 September.
